package_info.package_name: polyfill.io (CDN service, as used by npm packages such as create-polyfill-service-url, dynamic-polyfill, etc.)
package_info.package_manager: npm (and any web project embedding the CDN)
package_info.package_versions: All versions using cdn.polyfill.io after domain transfer to Funnull (Feb 2024 onward)
package_info.why_malicious: The polyfill.io CDN began serving malicious JavaScript after its domain was acquired by a new owner (Funnull). The CDN injected code that redirected mobile users to scam sites, affecting any website or npm package embedding scripts from cdn.polyfill.io. This constitutes a supply chain attack, as the malicious code was automatically delivered to all downstream consumers without their knowledge or consent.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when the script is loaded by the browser)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Detects if the visitor is using a mobile device by inspecting the user agent string. If a mobile device is detected, the code immediately redirects the user to an external scam website by assigning a new value to window.location.href.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code performs user-agent sniffing to identify mobile devices and then forcibly redirects those users to an external, non-affiliated domain. Such behavior is not expected in a polyfill library, which should only provide JavaScript feature compatibility. The redirect targets a scam site, indicating clear malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate polyfill library should only contain code for feature detection and shimming, not for user-agent checks or redirection. The presence of redirect logic in a third-party compatibility script is a direct violation of user trust and expected functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: User-agent checks and redirects are sometimes used in first-party code to direct mobile users to a mobile-optimized site. However, this is never appropriate in a third-party polyfill library loaded from a CDN, as it introduces a supply chain risk and violates the principle of least privilege.
key_indicators: User-agent sniffing for mobile device detection using regular expressions
Immediate assignment to window.location.href for forced navigation
Redirect destination is an external, non-affiliated, and likely malicious domain
Malicious logic embedded within a widely used third-party polyfill script
Behavior occurs at import-time, affecting all downstream consumers automatically

attack_chain.action: Website or npm package includes a script tag referencing cdn.polyfill.io (e.g., <script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v3/polyfill.min.js"></script>)
attack_chain.leads_to: Browser loads and executes the JavaScript from the CDN

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is delivered from the compromised CDN endpoint
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in the context of the website visitor

attack_chain.action: Malicious code checks if the visitor is on a mobile device and redirects them to a scam site
attack_chain.leads_to: User is sent to a phishing or scam site, potentially leading to credential theft, malware infection, or further compromise

behavioral_signatures: Third-party JavaScript performing user-agent sniffing and redirecting users based on device type
Unexpected window.location or document.location assignments in polyfill scripts
Polyfill scripts containing code unrelated to feature detection or shimming, such as DOM manipulation or network redirects
file_indicators: References to cdn.polyfill.io in script tags or npm package source code
Polyfill JavaScript files (e.g., polyfill.min.js) containing redirect logic or user-agent checks
network_indicators: Subsequent HTTP redirects to known scam or phishing domains from pages loading polyfill.io scripts
Unusual traffic patterns originating from polyfill.io script loads, especially on mobile devices
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for inclusion of cdn.polyfill.io in web pages or npm package dependencies. Analyze loaded JavaScript for unexpected behaviors such as user-agent checks and forced redirects. Use Content Security Policy (CSP) to block or report unexpected script sources. Employ Subresource Integrity (SRI) to ensure third-party scripts have not been tampered with. Flag any polyfill scripts that perform DOM manipulations, network requests, or redirections unrelated to polyfill functionality. Correlate user complaints or analytics spikes in mobile user drop-off with the presence of polyfill.io scripts.
